title: Solo dev, browser loot game now live: how I actually work with an AI coding agent
author: Professional-Emu4891
selftext:
I'm the dev of Arsenal Zero, a free browser collection game: you open crates, send your operator on timed expeditions and build a collection of military gear from Common to Mythic. It's been live with real players since October 13, and I built it solo with an AI coding agent (Claude Code) as my main tool. A few things about the workflow that might be useful to others here.

**I decide, the agent builds.** Game design, balance targets, art direction and every final call stay with me. The agent turns that into code fast: about 120k lines of TypeScript (Expo / React Native, running on the web), about 42k lines of SQL and 350+ database migrations on Supabase. Item rolls and rewards are computed server-side in Postgres functions so the client can't cheat. That kind of strict, rule-heavy code is where an agent really shines.

**Written rules beat good prompts.** The biggest jump in quality came from keeping project rules in writing, not from better prompts. For example: any breaking change on the server becomes a new function next to the old one, because dev and live share the same database. Every visible text goes through a translation key, so the game ships in French and English at the same time. Images come in two sizes, the large one only where it's actually needed. Once a rule is written down, I don't have to repeat it.

**Simulate before players do.** I had the agent build a headless simulator that plays the real game engine with six player profiles over 60 days, from casual to heavy spender. Before touching a reward or a drop rate, I run it and look at the curves. It's the best investment I made for balance.

**Generated, not just prompted.** All the sound effects are synthesized by a Python script with numpy, no samples. The colored haze behind each item card is generated the same way, one color per rarity. Cheap, light, and fully consistent across the game.

A question for those of you shipping with AI agents: **how do you keep the agent aligned with your project's rules over weeks of work?** Written rule files, memory, checklists, something else?

**The game is free and plays in the browser on phone or desktop, no download (optional purchases exist, hence the flair):** [**arsenalzero.com**](https://arsenalzero.com/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=aigamedev)

Happy to go into detail on any part of the workflow.
